Article Title: PM Modi sets Quad agenda, calls for 'concrete goals' to ensure Indo-Pacific security
Article Text:
File photo: Prime Minister Narendra Modi with US President Donald Trump, second right, Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, left, and Australia's Prime Minister Anthony Albanese during the Quad Leaders Meeting, in Manila

Trump calls PM Modi a 'tough man', 'great leader'

Quad meets amid shifting regional equations

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday described the Quad as a “constructive and trusted partnership” and called for concrete goals for its next phase of cooperation.Addressing US president Donald Trump, Japanese prime minister Sanae Takaichi and Australian prime minister Anthony Albanese, PM Modi said Manila had a special connection with the grouping, with officials from the four countries first meeting in the city in 2007. The Quad dialogue was revived there a decade later, in 2017.“It gives me immense pleasure to meet you all. Manila and Quad have shared an age-old and special bond,” PM Modi said, adding that the latest meeting in the Philippine capital marked an important milestone for the grouping.He noted that the foreign ministers of the four countries had met five times since January last year, describing this as evidence of their “political will and shared commitment” to the partnership.“For India, the Quad is a constructive and trusted partnership. From maritime security to trusted supply chains, new technologies to disaster response, it has been our endeavour that the Quad provides trusted solutions,” PM Modi said.The prime minister said he was confident the meeting would help set concrete goals for the next phase of cooperation. He also thanked the other leaders for their continued support and personal contributions to the partnership.During the meeting, Trump praised PM Modi, describing him as a friend and a leader respected around the world.“He is a tough man. He is my friend. He is a great leader and respected all over the world,” Trump said, adding that Washington and New Delhi had “outstanding relationships” and were coordinating closely.The Quad meeting was held on the sidelines of the Asean summit in Manila and marked the first leaders-level gathering of the four-nation grouping since September 2024.The meeting comes as Trump prepares to travel to China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit and talks with Chinese president Xi Jinping. The possibility of a meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin has also been raised.The Quad, comprising India, the US, Japan and Australia, has expanded its agenda beyond traditional security cooperation to include critical minerals, resilient supply chains, emerging technologies, infrastructure and disaster response.Maritime security, commercial shipping routes, access to vital minerals and cooperation in areas such as artificial intelligence and semiconductors are among the key areas of interest for the grouping.Ahead of the meeting, US secretary of state Marco Rubio said the Quad was not directed against any particular country, including China.For India, the summit is part of a wider diplomatic engagement with Southeast Asia. PM Modi is also attending the Asean-India and East Asia summits in Manila, where he is expected to discuss regional security, trade and connectivity.
Article Summary: Quad meeting was held on the sidelines of the Asean summit in Manila. It marked the first leaders-level gathering of the four-nation grouping since September 2024. PM Modi said he was confident the meeting would help set concrete goals for the next phase of cooperation.

Article Title: 'SP workers' names will be deleted': Akhilesh claims BJP trying to add fake voters to rolls
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav on Tuesday accused the BJP of attempting to add fake voters to Uttar Pradesh's electoral rolls ahead of the 2027 assembly elections. He alleged that the ruling party was using Form 6 applications to manipulate voter entries and warned that the names of SP workers and Opposition sympathisers could be deleted before polling.Speaking in Lucknow after the publication of the draft electoral roll, Yadav also alleged that the BJP was preparing to create discrepancies between the voter lists available with political parties and those used by presiding officers on polling day."The number should indeed increase, but we will have to be wary of conspiracies," he said, adding that the SP would examine the increase in voter numbers booth-wise.Responding to the Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer's press conference on the draft electoral roll, Yadav alleged that the BJP was attempting to influence the voter list by adding names of people from other states."The first question is that the CM had said 1.27 crore Hindu votes have been deleted. After that, this increase in number has begun. I can claim that the BJP and its underground-unregistered people are now ready.You would find the names of people from Bihar, MP, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh in the voter list," he said.Yadav also alleged that the BJP wanted differences between the electoral rolls distributed to political parties and the lists available with presiding officers at polling booths on election day."Names of sympathisers and workers of Opposition parties, especially the SP, will be deleted. You will find this on the last day. We will have to be careful," he said.In a separate post on X, Yadav accused the BJP and its allies of attempting to add bogus voters through applications under Form 6. He alleged that the exercise involved the categories of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate (ASDD) voters."The BJP and its conspiratorial allies, sensing their imminent defeat in Uttar Pradesh, are launching a special intelligence campaign to add fake votes under the ‘ASDD’ (Absent, Shifted, Dead, or Duplicate) designation," he wrote.Yadav said the SP had put in place a monitoring mechanism to track every new addition to the electoral roll. It would involve booth in-charges, PDA guards, declared and potential candidates, party functionaries, members, supporters and well-wishers.He said the monitoring would extend from individual polling booths to the Election Commission. The party had also asked citizens to keep track of new voter entries in their neighbourhoods."We will demand an accounting of every vote and will not allow any vote to be added if there is even the slightest bit of dishonesty," Yadav said.He warned that the party would collect evidence against officials allegedly involved in irregular additions and file complaints seeking action against them, including dismissal from service and withholding of pension and other benefits.Yadav's remarks came after Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa announced the publication of the draft electoral roll under the Special Summary Revision (SSR) 2027 on Tuesday.The claims and objections period will remain open from November 17 to December 16, allowing voters and other stakeholders to raise concerns over entries in the draft list.The revision comes ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, with the electoral roll likely to remain a key point of political contest between the ruling BJP and the Opposition SP.
Article Summary: Akhilesh Yadav warns that SP workers' names could be deleted before the 2027 polls. Yadav alleges that the ruling party was using Form 6 applications to manipulate voter entries. Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa announced the publication of the draft electoral roll on Tuesday.

US President Donald Trump on Tuesday praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a meeting with the leaders of the Quad grouping in Manila, describing him as a "tough man", a "great leader" and his friend, who is "respected all over the world"."He is a tough man," Trump said on PM Modi "He is my friend. His visit comes amid domestic challenges, including a major disruption to the US aviation industry and controversy surrounding Nvidia and its former chief executive Jensen Huang, who was linked to a woman alleged to be a Chinese government agent. Beijing has denied involvement.The Asean discussions are expected to focus on strengthening trade and security ties, as well as regional challenges, including the ongoing conflict in Myanmar and tensions in the South China Sea. The region has seen growing confrontations between Chinese and Philippine maritime forces over disputed waters, which are a key global trade route.The Quad, comprising the US, India, Japan and Australia, aims to counter China's growing influence in the Indo-Pacific. The Manila meeting is the grouping's first leaders' engagement since Trump returned to the White House last year.

NEW DELHI: Former Isro chairman S Somanath on Tuesday said India is aiming to increase its share in the global space economy to 8-9%, highlighting the need for stronger collaboration between the government and private sector to achieve the target.Speaking to reporters, Somanath said India's contribution to the global space economy was around 2% in 2020, when the sector was estimated to be worth approximately $550 billion. Article Title: 'Blatant and intentional': India slams Turkey over exclusion from UNGA draft consultations
Article Text:

India slammed Turkey at the United Nations for its "blatant and intentional" decision to exclude New Delhi and other member states from consultations on a resolution on cooperation between the UN and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC).India voted against the draft resolution, which was adopted by the UN General Assembly with 112 votes in favour, six against and 39 abstentions. Armenia, Cyprus, Greece, Israel and the US also voted against it. Iraq introduced the resolution, while Turkey served as its facilitator.India's deputy permanent representative to the UN Yojna Patel said the OIC's Permanent Observer Mission chose to exclude the Indian delegation and a number of other countries while circulating successive drafts of the resolution.While delivering India's explanation of vote, Patel also called for an investigation into the working methods adopted by the resolution's facilitator."My delegation has voted against this resolution not only because of its substantive aspects, but also for an even more concerning matter regarding the working methods adopted by the facilitator who convened negotiations on the same," Patel said."This is not only shocking but also sets a bad precedent of delegations excluding specific member states to enable their agendas," she added.Patel also said that despite some delegations registering their objections in subsequent rounds, the "facilitators still chose to not include select countries". Other basic procedures, such as acknowledging inputs, were also "blatantly disregarded", indicating that the exclusion was by design rather than by mistake.She said it was "unfortunate that there are member states who publicly profess commitment to multilateralism and completely turn a blind eye to its core guiding principles".Underlining that the UN was founded on the principles of sovereign equality, inclusivity and multilateral cooperation, Patel said differences of position among member states were inherent to multilateral diplomacy and "cannot, in themselves, justify blatant and intentional exclusion from the consultations on matters before the General Assembly"."My delegation strongly objects to such working methods that try to hoodwink excluded delegations into believing that this was just a technical update, which it was not," she said.In a thinly veiled reference to Pakistan , India also voiced regret that the OIC had "once again allowed itself to be systematically misused by one member state to weaponise OIC resolutions and declarations against India through false and baseless allegations".Pakistan is a founding and prominent member of the 57-member OIC.Greece and Cyprus also raised "serious concerns" regarding the conduct of negotiations under Turkiye's facilitation."Throughout the process, the European Union submitted comments and amendments in good faith, which were neither meaningfully addressed nor accompanied by substantial explanations for their rejection. Furthermore, revised drafts were circulated without adequate consultation," Greece's delegate said.
Article Summary: India voted against the draft resolution, which was adopted by the UN General Assembly with 112 votes in favour, six against and 39 abstentions. Armenia, Cyprus, Greece, Israel and the US also voted against it. Iraq introduced the resolution, while Turkey served as its facilitator.

Article Title: 'Paying price for being a woman, Muslim': Congress slams SC bail order in Bilkis Bano case
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Tuesday criticised the Supreme Court 's decision to suspend the life sentences of two convicts in the Bilkis Bano gangrape and murder case, saying she was being subjected to fresh "humiliation" and trauma.The party said the treatment meted out to her reflected the price women, particularly Muslim women, had to pay for seeking justice.Congress media and publicity department head Pawan Khera said Bilkis Bano had issued a statement expressing shock over the order, stating that she was neither informed of the proceedings nor given an opportunity to be heard. He added that she had announced her intention to challenge the decision."As if the cruel and gruesome crime committed against her was not enough, she is now being made to endure fresh humiliation and trauma. That is the price one has to pay for being a woman, and even more so for being a Muslim," Khera said in a post on X.In a statement issued through senior advocate Shobha Gupta, Bano said she learnt about the Supreme Court's October 28 order through media reports and questioned how the decision could have been taken without hearing her.She said this was the second time an order concerning the case had been passed without giving her an opportunity to present her views."I still cannot believe that once again, for the second time, an order has been passed by the Supreme Court without calling me up and without hearing me. I learnt of this through press reports," she said.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale suspended the life sentences of Bipin Chandra Joshi and Pradeep Mordhiya, granting them bail on October 28. The court noted that both convicts had spent more than 17 years in prison and that one of them had a severe handicap."Having heard the parties, suffice it to state that the appellants have been under incarceration for a period of more than 17 years, and also the fact remains that one of the appellants has a severe handicap. Certainly, there are issues to be decided in the appeal, both on fact and law," the court said in its order."In view of the above and considering the issues involved in this appeal, we suspend the sentence and grant bail to the appellants on such terms and conditions as may be imposed by the concerned trial court," it added.Bano was 21 years old and five months pregnant when she was gang-raped while fleeing the communal riots that broke out in Gujarat in February 2002 following the Godhra train burning incident. Her three-year-old daughter was among the seven family members killed.Joshi and Mordhiya were among the 11 men whose remission was quashed by the Supreme Court in 2024. Bano has said she will challenge the latest order granting bail to the two convicts.
Article Summary: Congress criticises Supreme Court's decision to suspend life sentences of two convicts in the Bilkis Bano gangrape and murder case. The party said the treatment meted out to Bano reflected the price women, particularly Muslim women, had to pay for seeking justice. Bano was 21 years old and five months pregnant when she was gang-raped while fleeing the communal riots in 2002.

Article Title: At Sonia's book launch, Gandhis open up about love, loss, and bad chicken
Article Text:
Sonia Gandhi's book launch on Monday.

NEW DELHI: "And listen, if you want to fall in love, go to Varsity Restaurant in Cambridge. But never eat the chicken chasseur, okay?" Rahul Gandhi jokingly delivered this piece of advice at the launch of his mother Sonia Gandhi 's memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love', in Delhi on Monday. Years after hearing the story about his parents' first meeting in Cambridge, he recounted how he went to the Varsity Restaurant with his girlfriend to see where they had met.When Rahul told the man at the entrance that his parents had met there, the man said he knew exactly who they were and recommended the chicken chasseur from the menu. However, the meal did not live up to its romantic legacy. Rahul contrasts his parents' memories of the restaurant with his own experience. "They seem to remember that the food was fantastic. The food's horrible!" he said as the audience laughed.The anecdote was part of a series of family recollections the leader of the opposition shared after saying he had been instructed to avoid politics. However, many read a political subtext into the seating arrangements. In the front row was an array of opposition leaders such as Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav; Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee; National Conference president Farooq Abdullah; Supriya Sule of NCP-SP; Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren; and Tamil Nadu CM C Joseph Vijay.Also in the front row was former Punjab CM Captain Amarinder Singh, who left Congress in 2021 following a bitter falling-out with the Gandhis.Rahul name-checked Amarinder and mentioned that he had seen his parents fight only once. Rajiv Gandhi was speaking to Amarinder on phone when Sonia tried several times to tell him something. Rajiv was stressed and eventually got angry. "We saw them argue many times, but that was the only time we ever saw them fight," Rahul said.Sonia Gandhi too kept the conversation away from politics. Asked why she chose to write a memoir when she had guarded her privacy fiercely in the past, she said she wanted to set the record straight about her family amid "unreal stories" woven around them. "So much has been said about my mother-in-law, husband, son, daughter, and myself; and most of it is unreal. It has really nothing to do with the way we are. Stories are woven around you, untruths are woven around you, and hurtful things are said which are nowhere near the truth. And I thought, well, perhaps this was a way of bringing out my feelings, what I know of my family, and maybe people will be open to listening to my story too," the Rajya Sabha MP said.She recalled feeling like an outsider when she first moved to India, conscious of making mistakes. She connected that experience to Indian women who enter a new family after marriage and have to adjust to its ways. The memoir's title, she said, reflected "the effort to be accepted and to belong, to finally belong."While she recounted a story of how she and Rajiv would go to India Gate to have ice cream (she had a favourite Sardarji ice cream vendor), Rahul spoke of his parents' affection and a habit he had assumed was common in every home: "Every meal there would be Papa and on Papa's lap there would be Mama." He said he realised it was unusual only when he visited friends' homes.But things changed after the assassinations of Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi, he said, "The fun-loving mother, the smiling mother disappeared." Sonia, once an extrovert, withdrew into herself.Rahul also spoke of his mother's resilience in the face of cancer, saying he had never seen her afraid or back down. He ended by telling her how proud he believed Rajiv would have been of her: "Mummy, Papa loved you. But I cannot even tell you how proud he would be of you."
Article Summary: Sonia Gandhi's memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love', launched in Delhi on Monday. She said she wanted to set the record straight about her family amid "unreal stories" woven around them. The memoir's title reflected "the effort to be accepted and to belong, to finally belong"

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Bilkis Bano said that "familiar fears are resurfacing" after the Supreme Court suspended the sentences and granted bail to two of the 11 men convicted of gang-raping her and murdering 14 members of her family during the 2002 Gujarat riots.In a statement issued on Monday, she expressed shock and disbelief over the order, saying she was neither informed about the proceedings nor given an opportunity to be heard."I still cannot believe that once again, for the second time, an order has been passed by the Supreme Court without calling me up and without hearing me. I learnt of this through press reports," she said.The Supreme Court bench of Justices M M Sudresh and P B Varale passed the order on October 28, which was uploaded on Monday. Reacting to the development, Bilkis said she was scared for herself, her family and her children, adding that the decision had shaken her faith in the justice system."For 24 years I have searched for and found reservoirs of courage I did not know I had, only because a million voices of support and solidarity came my way," she said, recalling her long fight for justice following the assault and the murder of her family members.Bilkis, who was 19 at the time of the 2002 incident, said she had spent years rebuilding her life with the support of family and friends and had hoped to find peace. However, the latest order had brought back the fears she thought she had overcome."Yet today I find myself losing the very justice I had fought so hard to win. Familiar fears are resurfacing. I am scared once again. For myself, my family, and my children. And I am scared of losing faith in justice, yet again," she said.Questioning why the court had not ensured that her voice was heard before passing the order, Bilkis said she would challenge the decision."I will fight this order. I must," she said, adding that she was doing so for her children and the memory of her three-year-old daughter Saleha, as well as for women everywhere."Because no woman, no survivor, no citizen should have to endure this eternal test of belonging and equality, and fight for justice for the rest of her life," she said.Bilkis Bano was 21 years old and five months pregnant when she was gang-raped while trying to escape the horror of the communal riots that broke out after the Godhra train burning incident in February 2002. Her three-year-old daughter was among the seven family members killed.
Article Summary: Bilkis Bano was gang-raped and 14 members of her family murdered during 2002 Gujarat riots. Supreme Court suspended the sentences and granted bail to two of the 11 men convicted of the crime. Bilkis said she was neither informed about the proceedings nor given an opportunity to be heard.

Article Title: Indian inventor patents new technique to transmute elements, reports gold in tests
Article Text:
Bengaluru inventor Rajah Vijay Kumar has patented a frequency-based process called GNT that he claims transmutes elements, with lab tests reporting gold and silver in processed samples

How it works

.

Larger ambition

BENGALURU: What if one chemical element could be converted into several others, including gold? An Indian inventor from Bengaluru has received a patent for a process that could do this using specially generated frequencies, without conventional nuclear reactors or radioactive reactions.There is no fission or fusion reaction here. His experiments report the presence of gold, silver and several other elements in processed samples.Rajah Vijay Kumar’s invention, called Gravitoradiophysical Nuclear Transmutation (GNT), has been granted Indian patent (No. 5683222), nearly eight years after it was filed on Nov 21, 2017. The patent was granted in the second half of 2025.“The GNT could eventually find applications in energy, medicine, genetics, industry and space,” Kumar, director and chief scientific officer, Scalene Energy Research Institute, Organization de Scalene Foundation, told TOI.To understand the process, it helps to know what makes one element different from another. Every element has atoms, and at the centre of each atom is a nucleus. The number of protons in this nucleus determines the element’s identity.Gold, for example, has 79 protons, while mercury has 80. Turning mercury into gold would therefore require changing the structure of its nucleus by removing (or displacing) one proton and one electron, something an ordinary chemical reaction cannot do.Kumar’s proposed process uses a specially designed reactor to achieve this. Its central component, called the ‘Boom Tube’, a tubular reactor that produces continuous free fall and weightlessness at molecular levels, fitted with antennas made from an aluminium alloy and connected to a high power high frequency generator. The apparatus also has systems to regulate temperature and pressure in a vacuum environment.The process works in two proposed stages. First, one frequency is used to separate the target element from the chemical compound containing it. A second frequency is then applied to bring about the proposed change in the element's nucleus.The process works in two proposed stages. First, a disassociating frequency depending on the interested elements is used to separate the target element from the chemical compound containing it. Then, an element specific transmutation frequency is then applied to bring about the proposed change in the element's nucleus. The exact mechanism of action is still being studied.As Kumar explains: “Every element has a unique frequency, or set of frequencies, that can break its chemical bonds and separate it from a compound. For the initial experiments, I chose mercury, which it describes as one of the heavier elements that could be handled relatively safely in its experimental setup. The aim, however, was not simply to make gold.”The larger ambition was to develop a process that can convert different elements and isotopes for possible applications in energy, medicine, industry and space exploration.The patent describes experiments in which a mercury compound, mercuric sulphate, was mixed with distilled water and processed through the reactor. An untreated portion was retained for comparison. An accredited laboratory, reportedly unaware of which samples had been processed, analysed both.The results reported gold at 1.91 mg per litre in the first processed sample and 2.3 milligrams per litre in the second. Silver was also detected at 11 milligrams per litre in the second test. Other elements, including magnesium, manganese, phosphorus and zinc, were reported in the processed samples. The mercury came down from 33.45 gm to 8.67 gm while sulphur almost remained unchanged at around 8.5 gm.The laboratory used a technique called Inductively Coupled Plasma Atomic Emission Spectroscopy (ICP-AES), which identifies and measures the quantities of elements in a sample. The research team acknowledges that considerable work under different conditions remains before the process can be perfected or considered for large-scale applications.There is also an important scientific caveat. Detecting gold, silver or other elements in a sample does not, by itself, mean the technology or process is ready for wider use immediately. The laboratory technique measures what is present, not how it was formed. Independent experiments, including tests of the elements’ atomic structure, would be needed to understand exactly the science of how such claimed transmutation has occurred.
Article Summary: Inventor Rajah Vijay Kumar has patented a frequency-based process called GNT that he claims transmutes elements. His experiments report the presence of gold, silver and several other elements in processed samples. Independent experiments, including tests of the elements’ atomic structure, would be needed to understand exactly how such claimed transmutation has occurred.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday said no voter or candidate had a right to demand reservation of a particular constituency for the SC/ST community, and govt's decision to reserve a constituency could not be questioned if the number of reserved constituencies was proportionate to these communities' population.The petitioners had challenged govt's 2025 amendment to Zilla Parishads and Panchayat Samitis Act, 1961. It is nobody's case that the required percentage of seats have not been reserved for the SC/ST community. "The bench refused to entertain the petition and said the amended rules conformed to the constitutionally mandated reservation policy. Article Title: A decade out of power: Why Congress is struggling to make a comeback in Uttarakhand
Article Text:
Congress enters the 2027 Uttarakhand election with growing support but deep organisational and leadership challenges, struggling to turn anti-incumbency into a credible alternative. (AI-generated image)

A state that once voted out its governments

The Harish Rawat question

Congress has plenty of issues, but no clear message

.

.

.

.

The BJP's vulnerabilities, and Congress's opportunity

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What will decide 2027?

Who leads the party in Uttarakhand?

What is its political alternative?

Can it rebuild its organisation?

"If you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear the result of a hundred battles. If you know yourself but not the enemy, for every victory gained you will also suffer a defeat. If you know neither the enemy nor yourself, you will succumb in every battle."The 'Art of War' by Sun Tzu seems to perfectly encapsulate what Congress needs to understand for the upcoming Uttarakhand assembly elections.The BJP , led in the state by chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, is seeking a historic third consecutive term. At a recent event in Dehradun, Union home minister Amit Shah set an ambitious target of winning more than 65 of the state's 70 assembly seats. The Congress, meanwhile, hopes to capitalise on dissatisfaction with the government and return to power after a decade in opposition.On paper, the Congress has a substantial list of issues to take to voters. The BJP, too, faces the challenge of defending its record in a state where the pendulum of power had previously been in constant swing.But the electoral arithmetic presents a more complicated picture as we saw in 2022.BJP can lose ground and still win comfortably; Congress can make gains and still remain distant from power.So, can Congress turn voter dissatisfaction into a legitimate political direction, or will it simply reiterate its criticisms and fail to make waves?Since the state was formed in 2000, its first four assembly elections produced a change of government every five years. The Congress won 36 seats in 2002, the BJP secured 35 in 2007, the Congress edged ahead with 32 against the BJP's 31 in 2012, and the BJP swept to power with 57 seats in 2017.And then came 2022, an election that broke the pattern and highlighted BJP’s growing strength in the state. BJP won 47 of the state's 70 seats, becoming the first party to secure consecutive terms since Uttarakhand's formation.But Congress had also made gains. Compared to 2017, its performance had improved from 11 seats to 19, while its vote share rose from approximately 33.5 per cent to nearly 38 per cent.The 2024 Lok Sabha election reinforced the challenge, with the BJP winning all five parliamentary constituencies in Uttarakhand. More significantly, Congress trailed in 63 of the state's 70 assembly segments, including 14 of the 19 constituencies it had won in 2022.Following the defeat, the Uttarakhand Pradesh Congress Committee tasked former minister Nav Prabhat with assessing the party's performance. The preliminary assessment identified a familiar set of problems: infighting, poor communication and a lack of coordination among party leaders.Congress had conducted similar reviews after its defeats in the 2014 and 2019 Lok Sabha elections and the 2017 and 2022 assembly elections. Yet the organisational weaknesses identified in those exercises continued to surface.Harish Rawat remains one of Congress's most recognisable figures in Uttarakhand, but his prominence has also been tied to the party's internal power struggles.Rawat was overlooked for the chief minister's post in 2002, despite the party emerging as the largest formation. After returning to power in 2012, Congress was hit by a major crisis in 2016, when nine MLAs rebelled against his government, triggering President's Rule and a prolonged political and legal battle. Several rebels later joined the BJP.The mistrust has persisted in the run-up to 2027. The controversy involving Gaurav Kumar, an alleged conman posing as Rahul Gandhi's private secretary, exposed tensions within the state unit. Bhavna Pandey alleged that Kumar demanded Rs 2–3 crore, claiming the central leadership wanted state president Ganesh Godiyal replaced. Godiyal alleged a conspiracy, while Rawat denied any political plot and called for a police probe.Personal rivalries, including Rawat's falling-out with former aide Ranjeet Rawat, have added to the uncertainty. The November reshuffle distributed key responsibilities among senior leaders, but whether it can contain competing ambitions remains unclear.Congress's challenge is to draw on Harish Rawat's experience and support base without allowing the campaign to become another contest over leadership.The Congress has sought to make women's safety and accountability central to its criticism of the government. Garima Mehra Dasauni, the party's chief spokesperson in Uttarakhand, said Congress has compiled a list of alleged crimes against women involving senior BJP leaders in the state.Dasauni also argues that the BJP's electoral success cannot be understood simply through its development claims.In her assessment, religious and communal mobilisation, alongside welfare measures, has helped the party consolidate support. She also points to the political value of ration distribution and other welfare schemes, particularly among economically vulnerable households.This raises an important question for the Congress: how does it challenge welfare politics without appearing to dismiss the benefits that people receive?Welfare politics is not new to the Congress either. The National Food Security Act, which made access to subsidised foodgrains a legal entitlement, was enacted in 2013 under the Congress-led United Progressive Alliance government. However, the BJP has made welfare delivery a key component of its electoral strategy, raising questions about how the Congress can distinguish its own welfare agenda from that of the ruling party.The challenge for Congress, political observers suggest, is not a shortage of issues to raise but the absence of a common thread that ties them together and presents voters with a clear alternative.Political scientist Hilal Ahmed explains:"The Congress is raising all these issues but they lack a narrative between them. What connects their concerns? BJP can easily answer all these separate claims."For the Congress, this creates a difficult strategic choice. It must distinguish itself from the BJP, but it cannot assume that voters will automatically respond to a campaign built around governance failures and economic grievances.Ahmed describes the Congress as having “a little bit of a victimhood mentality” and calls it “intellectually weak”. He also warns that its response to the BJP remains fragmented rather than forming a coherent and constructive critique.His assessment of the potential electoral consequences is stark: “BJP might not win but neither will Congress.”The BJP's position in Uttarakhand is stronger than the Congress's current organisational condition. Combining the appeal of PM Modi, CM Dhami’s work on ground and the promise of continuity through the double-engine government, it seeks to retain its position.The BJP will also seek to hold together a broad social coalition, while appealing to women, young voters, ex-servicemen and the Sikh community. Its reported plans for younger candidates and greater emphasis on local feedback suggest an effort to refresh its organisation.At the same time, the party is linking voter-list revision to its rhetoric around identity and belonging. At a Dehradun meeting, BJP leader Bhatt urged workers to remove those described as “infiltrators”, saying: “Only the original people of Devbhoomi should decide the government.”One of the most important arguments in Ahmed's analysis concerns the state's economic and social structure.Migration is not simply a consequence of unemployment; it also reflects the concentration of education, healthcare, transport and jobs in towns and the plains.Ahmed argues that Congress has failed to develop a convincing response to the BJP's rhetoric around identity. It could challenge the government's economic priorities and what he describes as a decade of policy paralysis, but must offer more than general claims about unemployment.The Dhami government's record offers Congress several openings: the Ankita Bhandari case and continuing questions over the alleged VIP angle, recruitment paper leaks, unemployment, migration, land rights and allegations of corruption.But identifying these vulnerabilities is easier than turning them into electoral support. Congress must show how it would address them, particularly concerns over employment, regional inequality and the protection of local land rights. The Uttarakhand Kranti Dal's attempt to revive the politics of statehood could also put pressure on Congress to articulate a stronger regional agenda.The party has begun preparing through leadership meetings, multiple Parivartan Yatras, village outreach and a campaign against the government's record.As Ahmed argues, Congress also has a lot of “professional politicians” — leaders who pursue political stature and may abandon Congress in the face of defeat, a scenario reminiscent of 2016.The BJP is approaching the election with the advantages of incumbency and a well-established organisation, but it is not without vulnerabilities.The Congress, meanwhile, has a substantial list of issues with which to challenge the government. But none of these issues will automatically produce a victory.The Congress needs to answer three questions.The art of war is also the art of elections. The Congress is yet to demonstrate that it understands both itself and its electoral 'enemy'.
Article Summary: Congress enters the 2027 Uttarakhand election with growing support but deep organisational and leadership challenges. The BJP, led in the state by chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, is seeking a historic third consecutive term. The Congress, meanwhile, hopes to capitalise on dissatisfaction with the government.

Article Title: Parents fled Mozambique with unregistered newborn; 26 yrs later, Gujarat woman gets Indian passport
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A 26-year-old woman from Gujarat, whose Indian parents brought her to the country as an unregistered newborn while fleeing floods in Mozambique, has finally received an Indian passport after a prolonged citizenship battle. Dolly Vadalia received the passport on November 11, following a Union home ministry memorandum recognising her as an Indian citizen, news agency PTI reported citing her brother-in-law Ronak Vadalia on Monday.Born on February 18, 2000, in Xai-Xai, Mozambique, Dolly was just 18 to 20 days old when her parents evacuated her from the country after a tropical cyclone triggered massive floods. The family returned to India and settled in Rajkot, their hometown.Dolly's citizenship status became a hurdle after she married Khilankumar Vadalia, a Rajkot resident employed in Canada, in 2023. Her inability to obtain an Indian passport kept the couple separated.Her three passport applications, filed in 2023 and 2025, were rejected because she could not establish her Indian citizenship through the required documents. Authorities sought proof of cancellation of her emergency certificate or consular registration of her birth.The matter was subsequently taken up with Lok Sabha MPs Ramesh Dhaduk and Parshottam Rupala, who forwarded it to the Rajkot collectorate, the Gandhinagar secretariat, the MHA and the MEA, Ronak said as cited by PTI.The MEA sought the MHA's opinion. In October last year, the home ministry reiterated that under Section 4(1)(b) of the Citizenship Act, 1955, a child born outside India must have their birth registered at an Indian consulate within one year to claim citizenship by descent. Although Dolly had an Aadhaar card, it was not sufficient to establish her eligibility for an Indian passport, Ronak said.On April 30 this year, a single-judge bench of the Gujarat high court observed that Dolly's parents had not followed the mandatory birth registration procedure. It held that she was neither an Indian citizen by birth nor by descent under Sections 3 and 4 of the Act."The court advised us to apply for citizenship; however, we could not file an application initially because we lacked a valid passport — a mandatory requirement for the process," Ronak said, explaining why the family subsequently approached a division bench.Following a background check and verification, the Indian embassy in Mozambique and the MHA issued a memorandum."Based on this, Dolly's birth was registered with the Indian High Commission in Maputo, Mozambique, in November. Using that certificate, we applied for a passport, which we finally received last week," he said.
Article Summary: Dolly Vadalia received the passport on November 11, following a Union home ministry memorandum recognising her as an Indian citizen. Born on February 18, 2000, in Xai-Xai, Mozambique, her parents evacuated her from the country after a tropical cyclone triggered massive floods. Her inability to obtain an Indian passport kept the couple separated.

Article Title: '520 drains discharge wastewater in the Yamuna': SC raps admin over rising pollution despite huge spending
Article Text:
SC says Yamuna pollution has worsened despite heavy spending and directs CPCB to monitor water quality across state and district boundaries

Authorities to face penalties for worsening water quality

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Monday pulled up civic authorities and Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) over the worsening pollution in the Yamuna despite large sums being spent on cleaning the river. The bench of Justices Manoj Misra and Manmohan directed CPCB to monitor water quality where the river and 520 drains enter and exit states, Union territories and districts.It also said authorities would be held accountable if water quality deteriorates in their jurisdiction, news agency PTI reported citing an order dated November 4. The matter has been listed for further hearing on January 13."This court is of the opinion that everything that is wrong with the civic administration in towns, cities and villages situated along the banks of the river is reflected in the poor health of the river and in the 520 drains that discharge wastewater into the Yamuna. This is why, despite huge sums being spent on cleaning the river, pollution in the Yamuna has only increased," the bench saidThe court said industrial pollutants and untreated sewage must be stopped at the source. It observed that building more sewage treatment plants alone would not be enough to address the problem.The bench said sewage should first be tapped and then treated wherever pollution cannot be prevented at the source. However, it flagged the difficulty of doing so because of weak sewage networks and the mixing of stormwater and sewage drains."Where that is not possible, the sewage must first be tapped and then treated.However, tapping will remain a challenge in absence of a robust sewage system and due to joining of stormwater and sewage drains. This court is further of the opinion that it would be difficult, if not impossible, for civic authorities to tap sewage in most illegal and unauthorised colonies built on encroached land, since they have not been built on a grid layout and have hardly any space for laying a sewage system," it said.The Supreme Court directed the CPCB to track water quality at the entry and exit points of states, Union territories and districts. If the water deteriorates on any parameter while passing through a jurisdiction, the concerned administration will be held accountable and penalised."If the water quality deteriorates on any parameter while flowing through, or exiting a state/Union territory or a district therein, that state/Union territory or district... shall be held accountable and penalised. The said compensation/ fine shall be deposited with the registry of this court," the bench said.The court asked the CPCB to propose a formula for calculating the compensation or fine.It also directed the board to investigate incidents indicating pollution in the river, including fish deaths, white foam on the surface, eutrophication or algal blooms, and spikes in biochemical oxygen demand (BOD), chemical oxygen demand (COD) or total suspended solids (TSS).The CPCB's reports must identify the causes of such incidents or increases in pollution levels and recommend remedial measures, the court said.The bench further directed central and state ministries, departments and agencies to provide the CPCB and its experts with administrative, technical, logistical and operational support.Public and private entities involved in wastewater, solid waste and effluent treatment have also been asked to provide CPCB officials and designated third-party agencies unrestricted access to their premises, installations and records. This includes access for surprise inspections, sample collection, audits and checks of monitoring equipment.The court said plant operators and concerned authorities must also provide complete data access and cooperate with the integration of their systems into the CPCB's centralised monitoring network.
Article Summary: Justices Manoj Misra and Manmohan directed CPCB to monitor water quality where the river and 520 drains enter and exit states, Union territories and districts. It said authorities would be held accountable if water quality deteriorates in their jurisdiction. The matter has been listed for further hearing on January 13.

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Monday constituted screening committees for five states scheduled to hold assembly elections, with party president Mallikarjun Kharge appointing senior leaders to head the panels. VADODARA: Bilkis Bano has said she will challenge the Supreme Court 's October 28 order suspending the sentences and granting bail to two of the 11 men convicted of gang-raping her and murdering 14 members of her family during the 2002 Gujarat riots In a statement issued through senior advocate Shobha Gupta, she expressed shock and disbelief that the order was passed without informing her or giving her an opportunity to be heard.Bilkis said she learnt about the development through press reports and questioned how the Supreme Court could pass such an order without ensuring that her voice was heard. For the past 24 years, she said, she had fought repeatedly for justice, not only for herself but also for women everywhere.She said she had discovered reserves of courage she never knew she possessed, largely because of the support and solidarity extended by a million voices. She recalled walking from one courtroom to another and being grateful each time she was vindicated and her faith in the idea of justice was restored.Bilkis said she had gradually rebuilt her life with the love and support of family and friends, yearned for peace and learnt to smile. However, the latest order had left her feeling that she was losing the very justice she had fought so hard to secure.She said familiar fears had resurfaced and she was scared once again for herself, her family and her children. She also expressed apprehension about losing faith in the justice system yet again.Questioning the decision to suspend the sentences of the men convicted in the case, she asked how the court could have passed the order without informing her or ensuring that she was heard."I will fight this order. I must," she said, adding that her fight was for her children, who did not deserve to remain haunted by the fears and scars of the past for the rest of their lives.She also invoked the memory of her three-year-old daughter Saleha, who was killed during the 2002 violence, saying she deserved to live and that her memory demanded justice.Bilkis said her fight was also for women everywhere, asserting that no woman, survivor or citizen should have to endure an eternal test of belonging and equality or spend the rest of her life fighting for justice.

Article Title: Cyclone Akvan: IMD warns of extremely heavy rainfall, 145 kmph winds along Andhra coast

Cyclonic Storm Akvan, currently positioned over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal, is expected to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm by the morning of November 19 before making landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast around noon on November 20, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said on Tuesday.According to the IMD's national bulletin issued at 2:30 am IST on November 17, the storm remained nearly stationary over the previous nine hours and continued to be centred over the same region.The weather system was located near latitude 12.2°N and longitude 85.7°E, around 610 km east of Chennai in Tamil Nadu, 630 km northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, 660 km southeast of Machilipatnam in Andhra Pradesh, 670 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 790 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha, according to the news agency ANI.The IMD said the storm is likely to move north-northwestwards and strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by the evening of November 17.It is subsequently expected to continue moving northwestwards and intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm by the morning of November 19.According to the forecast, the system will continue its northwestward movement before crossing the Andhra Pradesh and yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni around noon on November 20.At the time of landfall, the cyclone is expected to generate maximum sustained wind speeds of 120-130 kmph, with gusts reaching up to 145 kmph, the bulletin stated.The IMD has issued an orange alert for the Andhra Pradesh coast and adjoining coastal areas of south Odisha, warning of the potential impact of the approaching cyclone.The weather department has forecast light to moderate rainfall at several places across north Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal on November 17 and 20, with isolated areas likely to receive heavy rainfall.Heavy to very heavy rainfall is also expected at isolated places on November 18 and 19, potentially causing waterlogging in parts of Tamil Nadu.For coastal Andhra Pradesh, the IMD has predicted light to moderate rainfall at several locations, accompanied by heavy showers at isolated places on November 18.The situation could intensify on November 19 and 20, with isolated areas of north coastal Andhra Pradesh likely to receive extremely heavy rainfall exceeding 21 cm.In Odisha, isolated areas are likely to experience heavy rainfall on November 18, with light to moderate showers expected at some places.The IMD has further forecast light to moderate rainfall across most places in the state, along with heavy to very heavy showers at isolated locations between November 19 and 21.The weather department's latest warning indicates that the approaching cyclone could bring intense rainfall and strong winds to several coastal districts, particularly in Andhra Pradesh and adjoining regions.
Article Summary: Cyclonic Storm Akvan is currently positioned over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal. It is expected to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm by the morning of November 19 before making landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast around noon on November 20.

Banerjee appeared before Kolkata Police on Saturday in connection with a fresh FIR registered at Girish Park Police Station on October 31 over his alleged remarks against the police.After leaving Bhawanipore Police Station, Banerjee said he had “nothing to hide” and maintained that he had responded to police summons in the past and would continue to do so.“I have nothing to hide. In the past too, whenever they have summoned me, I have gone. If they summon me in the future, I will go,” he told reporters.He also said he would not be intimidated by police action, adding: “Use whatever power you have; put all your strength. Put me in jail, strangle me, but this head will not bow before anyone.”Kolkata Police had served Banerjee a notice asking him to appear before the investigating officer on November 20 in connection with the FIR, according to news agency ANI.The complaint concerns alleged remarks made by the TMC MP against the police.
Article Summary: Calcutta High Court issues show-cause notice to TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee. Justice Krishna Rao held that Banerji's statements and a social media post against the court amounted to “ex facie criminal contempt” Justice Rao directed the Diamond Harbour MP to explain within 15 days of the notice being issued.

NEW DELHI: Delhi water minister Parvesh Sahib Singh claimed on Tuesday that no froth was present anywhere along the 52-km section of the Yamuna that passes through the national capital.Speaking at a press conference, Singh dismissed allegations by the Aam Aadmi Party that devotees had been made to observe Chhath Puja at spots where the river was covered in froth.“Seeing that the BJP has won the hearts of Purvanchali people, AAP is pained,” Singh said, as per PTI.“Chhath was celebrated with a lot of reverence and lakhs of people were so happy with the preparations,” he added.However, Singh noted that the Delhi government was in talks with Uttar Pradesh to tackle the issue in areas near the Okhla Barrage, which lies on the UP-Delhi border.The Okhla Barrage is often highlighted for the recurring formation of toxic froth on the Yamuna's surface.According to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), monitoring conducted at Kalindi Kunj, downstream of the Okhla Barrage, between 2022 and 2024 found that the sudden fall of water from the barrage agitates foaming agents present in wastewater, causing foam to form and float on the Yamuna's surface.Surfactants found in detergents are the main foaming agents in untreated or partially treated sewage.Separately, a study titled Study on Yamuna Frothing in Delhi, conducted by the Energy and Resources Institute (Teri) for the Delhi government's environment department, identified poor water quality as the primary trigger for froth formation. It pointed to factors including effluents containing high levels of ammonia and phosphate released from anionic surfactants.
Article Summary: Delhi water minister Parvesh Sahib Singh claimed on Tuesday that no froth was present anywhere along the 52-km section of the Yamuna that passes through the national capital. Singh dismissed allegations by the Aam Aadmi Party that devotees had been made to observe Chhath Puja at spots where the river was covered in froth.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday agreed to hear on Wednesday a plea filed by the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) seeking contempt action against a lawyer who allegedly made unsavoury remarks against Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant during court proceedings.The plea was mentioned for urgent listing before a bench comprising the CJI and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana. SCBA secretary Pragya Baghel and joint secretary Meenesh Dubey mentioned the matter before the bench.They informed the court that the association had obtained the consent of Attorney General R Venkataramani to file a petition seeking the initiation of criminal contempt proceedings against the lawyer.The development follows an incident on Monday, when the lawyer was escorted out of a Supreme Court courtroom after allegedly making unsubstantiated and unsavoury remarks against the CJI.The incident began when the lawyer made an unscheduled mention of a petition filed on November 2, claiming it had not been listed despite the CJI's office being informed.The bench was hearing motor accident compensation cases at the time.The court objected to the unscheduled mention and asked the lawyer to approach the registrar to have his request for early listing included.The lawyer said he had already apologised and wanted to know why the petition had not been listed. When the CJI said he would look into the matter, the lawyer allegedly reacted by questioning his position and integrity.“No, I will not wait. You cannot sit in that chair. You do not deserve. You do not have the integrity for that,” the lawyer told the CJI.A registry official said that petitions were listed through court software and that the CJI had little role in the process.The official also said several petitions had been filed before November 6, after which the court remained closed for a week for Diwali.The lawyer's conduct drew objections from members of the Bar, some of whom met the CJI and requested that contempt proceedings be initiated against him.The SCBA has now moved to seek criminal contempt action, with its office-bearers informing the Supreme Court that they had secured the Attorney General's consent to file the plea.The matter is scheduled to be heard on Wednesday.

Article Title: NMC asks all government medical colleges, attached hospitals to join road accident cashless treatment scheme
Article Text:
NMC has asked deans, directors, principals and medical superintendents to accord priority to the exercise and take necessary steps to facilitate their institutions’ participation.

NEW DELHI: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has directed all government medical colleges and their attached hospitals across the country to onboard the Centre’s PM-RAHAT scheme, aimed at ensuring cashless treatment for road accident victims during the critical golden hour.In a public notice issued on Monday, the NMC has asked deans, directors, principals and medical superintendents to accord priority to the exercise and take necessary steps to facilitate their institutions’ participation. The move follows a request from the Union Health Ministry’s Trauma and Burn Cell to the commission on October 28 to widen the network of hospitals under the scheme.The PM-RAHAT (Prime Minister’s Road Accident Victims’ Hospitalisation and Assured Treatment) scheme provides cashless treatment of up to Rs 1.5 lakh per accident victim for a maximum of seven days from the date of the accident at designated hospitals. Non-designated hospitals can provide stabilisation treatment to victims, ensuring that emergency care is not delayed while patients are referred to higher-level facilities.The guidelines issued by the National Health Authority (NHA) provide for two categories of hospitals under the scheme: designated hospitals, which can provide stabilisation, trauma and polytrauma services, and PM-RAHAT Lite hospitals, which can provide initial stabilisation before referring patients to higher-level facilities.Hospitals empanelled under Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY will be deemed eligible for designation. Other hospitals can also join, provided they meet the prescribed infrastructure and clinical requirements. These include round-the-clock emergency services, an equipped ICU, emergency operation theatre, imaging facilities, blood storage and ambulance services.The guidelines also prioritise hospitals located near accident-prone stretches, including national and state highways, identified road accident hotspots and municipal roads.The scheme was launched by the Prime Minister on February 13, 2026, with the objective of removing financial barriers to emergency treatment and strengthening trauma care across the country.
Article Summary: The PM-RAHAT (Prime Minister’s Road Accident Victims’ Hospitalisation and Assured Treatment) scheme provides cashless treatment of up to Rs 1.5 lakh per accident victim. Non-designated hospitals can provide stabilisation treatment to victims, ensuring that emergency care is not delayed.
